newsitem.title: UK: Ford sticks to UK job cuts after union talks.
newsitem.headline: Ford sticks to UK job cuts after union talks.

text.p: Ford said on Thursday it was sticking to plans to make 1,300 workers redundant at its Halewood plant in northeastern England.
In a statement after talks with unions, Ford said the Escort model would continue to be built at Halewood until the year 2000, after which the plant would produce a new, Escort based car.
Unions said earlier they would hold a strike ballot in protest at the job cuts.
Ford said it had agreed to the union's request to meet Jac Nasser, President of Ford Automtive Operations and Chairman of Ford of Europe, to discuss the situation at Halewood.
Ford said the time and place of the meeting had yet to be determined, although the Transport and General Workers Union said it expected the meeting to be held in London in the next few days.

Ford's statement said: "At today's meeting Ford reiterated that from the year 2000 Halewood would become the European source for a planned new Escort based vehicle, subject to appropriate product and investment approvals and to competitive levels of performance being achieved at Halewood."
It added: "The company also confirmed that Halewood would continue to produce the present model Escort car through to the year 2000."
Ford said the planned 1,300 redundancies, out of a workforce of about 4,500, would be voluntary.

Ford's European Vehicle Operations manager, David Gorman, said: "The actions we have announced for Halewood Assembly Operations give the plant a realistic future with an exciting new Escort based vehicle in the medium term, subject to approvals and to performance objectives being reached."
At the talks, union leaders had been attempting to persuade Ford to reverse the job cut plans. --London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
